content:
Oddness gives \(f(0)=0\). Period \(2\) gives \(f(-1)=f(1)\), while oddness gives \(f(-1)=-f(1)\). Hence \(f(1)=0\). By period \(2\), every integer is a zero.

Thus \(f(x)\) has at least the zeros
\[
0,1,2,\dots,2009
\]
in \([0,2009]\), which are \(2010\) zeros.

This is attainable, e.g. \(f(x)=\sin(\pi x)\), which is odd, period \(2\), and has zeros exactly at integers.

\[
\boxed{2010}
\]
